title: High molecular weight DNA extraction from fungal spores for long read sequencing
author: Nonthakorn (Beatrice) Apirajkamol

steps.title: Prepare lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Make fresh cell lysis buffer containing 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.5, 50 mM EDTA, 5 % SDS, and 1 % 2‑mercaptoethanol.

steps.title: Add beads and buffer to tube
steps.instruction: In a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube add 250 µL of 1.0 mm zirconia (ceramic) beads (suitable for fungal spores 2–3.5 µm) and 600 µL of the freshly prepared cell lysis buffer.

steps.title: Add spore sample
steps.instruction: Add approximately 50–200 mg of fungal spores to the tube.

steps.title: Homogenise spores
steps.instruction: Homogenise with a tissue homogeniser at 5,000 rpm for 15 seconds.

steps.title: Pellet cell debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at high speed (≥19,000 g) for 10–15 minutes (or longer if required) to precipitate cell debris.

steps.title: Add proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL of Proteinase K (20 mg/mL, Invitrogen, cat. #25530049) to the supernatant and vortex briefly.

steps.title: Transfer cleared lysate
steps.instruction: Collect the supernatant and transfer it to a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, avoiding the debris pellet.

steps.title: Incubate for protein digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 56–57 °C for a maximum of 3 hours or until the mixture becomes clear.

steps.title: Add RNase A
steps.instruction: Add 3 µL of RNase A (100 mg/mL, Qiagen, cat. #19101) and incubate at 37 °C for 5 minutes. (If different enzyme concentrations are used, adjust volumes according to the manufacturer’s recommendation.)

steps.title: Cool to room temperature
steps.instruction: Cool the reaction to 22–24 °C (room temperature).

steps.title: Add sodium acetate
steps.instruction: Add half the volume of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) to the supernatant to precipitate protein.

steps.title: Vortex to cloud
steps.instruction: Vortex for 30 seconds, ensuring the mixture becomes cloudy.

steps.title: Pellet protein precipitate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 5–10 minutes at high speed (≥19,000 g) until the supernatant shows no visible debris or protein.

steps.title: Transfer cleared supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer the clear supernatant to a new tube, avoiding the precipitated protein pellet.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of isopropanol (≥99.8 %) to the supernatant, invert the tube 10 times, and do NOT vortex.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA pellet in TE
steps.instruction: Add 20–50 µL of TE buffer (Invitrogen, cat. #12090015) and let the DNA pellet resuspend either at room temperature overnight or at 56 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Dry to remove alcohol
steps.instruction: Dry the tube to eliminate alcohol residue by leaving it at room temperature for 1 hour or in a heat block at 56 °C for no longer than 15 minutes.

steps.title: Remove supernatant and dry tube
steps.instruction: Remove any remaining supernatant and dry the tube over absorbent paper as described in the previous drying step.

steps.title: Centrifuge after drying
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube for 10–15 minutes at high speed (≥19,000 g).

steps.title: Wash DNA pellet with ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 1000 µL of freshly made 70 % w/v (80 % v/v) ethanol (derived from ≥99.5 % undenatured ethanol), invert the tube gently 10 times, and do NOT vortex.

steps.title: Remove ethanol and dry pellet
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, remove the ethanol supernatant without disturbing the DNA pellet; then invert the tube over clean absorbent paper to dry the pellet.

steps.title: Final centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube for 10–15 minutes at high speed (≥19,000 g) to collect the dried DNA pellet.
